static renderMarkdown(string $markdown, ?Theme $theme = null): stringTop-level convenience: render Markdown with a one-shot Renderer instance and return the ANSI string. Mirrors glamour's package-level Render function.
static cached(?Theme $theme = null, ?int $width = null): selfThe shared renderer for $theme at $width columns, built on first use and returned as the same instance after that. A caller that renders on every frame (a TUI pane, a chat transcript) gets one parser, one Environment and one stylesheet for the whole session instead of paying for them per frame (rank 39). Null $theme means Theme::ansi(); null $width means no wrapping.
write(string $markdown, mixed $output = STDOUT): intRender Markdown and write the ANSI output straight to a stream (default STDOUT). Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour's package-level Write function.
stream(iterable $chunks): \GeneratorIncremental render channel: consumes Markdown input as a stream of string chunks and yields styled ANSI chunks as complete top-level block sections finish — the sugar-ecosystem port of glamour's render-then-print block-by-block intent, so a caller can forward bytes while the tail of the document is still arriving.
defersStreaming(): boolTrue when this renderer's document-scope post-processing (block prefix/suffix, indent, margin, preservedNewLines) is global by nature, forcing the streaming family (stream(), Writer) to buffer the whole document into its final chunk. Single source of the law so both channels can never diverge on the predicate.
writer(StreamSink $sink): WriterWrite-side counterpart of stream(): an object channel that accepts Markdown chunks through Writer::feed() and pushes every newly proven section into the sink immediately (write-through flush law). Shares the section stream and deferral predicate with this channel, so feed()/close() output equals stream() output for the same bytes.
renderSection(string $section): stringRender one section to its raw ANSI body WITHOUT the document-scope post-processing of render(): no rtrim, block prefix/suffix, indent, or margin — those wrap the assembled stream exactly once (and when they are configured at all, stream() falls back to buffering).
static fromEnvironment(?Theme $default = null): selfBuild a Renderer whose theme is selected by the GLAMOUR_STYLE environment variable. Unset or unrecognised falls back to $default — and to Theme::ansi() when no default was supplied (SM-S33: the caller's fallback was previously forced to be ansi, which could not be expressed through this door). Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour.RenderWithEnvironmentConfig.
withTheme(Theme $theme): self
withWordWrap(?int $cols): selfWrap paragraph + blockquote + list-item bodies at $cols cells. Headings, code blocks and tables are never wrapped (they carry their own width semantics; heading passthrough matches glamour). Pass null to disable wrapping; 0 or a negative count throws.
withHyperlinks(bool $on = true): selfEmit OSC 8 hyperlink escapes for [text](url) links so terminals that support it render the text as a real clickable link. When disabled (or the terminal doesn't support OSC 8), links degrade to styled text plus a trailing (url) suffix. Default: enabled.
withBaseURL(?string $url): selfBase URL prefixed onto relative [text](path) link / image targets. URLs that already have a scheme (http://, https://, mailto:, …) pass through unchanged. Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour.WithBaseURL.
withTableWrap(bool $on = true): selfWrap text inside table cells at the renderer's word-wrap width. Default off (cells render unwrapped, matching glamour's default). Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour.WithTableWrap.
withInlineTableLinks(bool $on = true): selfWhether links inside table cells render as inline [text](url) pairs (default — terse, scannable) or as full hyperlinks. When false, table cells suppress the trailing (url) and OSC-8 envelope since they bloat narrow columns — which discards the destination ENTIRELY: probe | [x](https://e.com) | with the flag off and every byte of the URL is gone from the output (no visible text, no envelope), not demoted to plain text. Glamour instead collects the destinations below the table as a footnote-style appendix; adopting that here is the owner-gated behaviour alternative (table bytes shift, a theme slot is needed), so the loss stands on the port's own terms — dated note 2026-11 (sugar-markdown-079). Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour.WithInlineTableLinks.
withTableColumnBudget(bool $on = true): selfBound a table's TOTAL rendered width by giving every column its share of the renderer's word-wrap width. Natural column contents are scaled down proportionally, floor one cell per column, until padding, border rules and all columns together fit withWordWrap($cols); each cell is then CLIPPED to its column budget. Default off — legacy withTableWrap per-cell full-width reflow is untouched.
withFenceColumnBudget(bool $on = true): selfClip fenced-code lines to the renderer's word-wrap width (the fence half of the bounded-geometry pair). withTableColumnBudget() bounds the one block kind whose geometry it can shrink by redistributing columns; a fence has no columns to shrink, so its long lines simply overflow the pane today. This is the block-clip the table budget leaves for fences: with the option on (default OFF — every existing byte snapshot holds), each rendered fence line is Width::truncateAnsi()-clipped at the current block stack's available width, on both the plain code-block and the syntax-highlighted paths. Content clipped here is the consumer's scroll/pager territory, exactly the bounded-geometry-now / full-content-later trade the column budget makes for tables. Indented code blocks are NOT touched — the entry scopes the FENCED half only.
withLineNumbers(bool $on = true): selfPrefix every line of a SYNTAX-HIGHLIGHTED fence with its 1-based number in a padded gutter (default OFF — every existing byte snapshot holds). Mirrors glamour's code-block line_number decoration; the gutter number rides the theme's muted comment slot and joins the code with SyntaxHighlighter::GUTTER_SEPARATOR — a measurable 1-cell box rule plus a space, never a bare tab (2026-11, SM-S34: candy-code's DiffGutter documents why a tab cannot survive a width-measured frame). The gutter interacts with withFenceColumnBudget(): numbers consume the budget — with both on, a clip can start eating the gutter itself once the number column exceeds the available width, so pair the flag with a wrap width that leaves room for it.
withStyleSheet(StyleSheet $sheet): selfUse a caller-supplied block cascade instead of StyleSheet::base() (M7). The sheet styles whole block kinds per nesting depth; the renderer seeds it fresh at each channel entry, so the default (null) keeps every existing byte. Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour's cascade option (element style maps).
withFolds(array $headingIds): selfFold the sections under the top-level headings named by $headingIds. A folded heading renders its own line, then a fold marker, and the blocks after it are hidden up to the next heading of any level. The hidden blocks are the body only: a heading nested under a folded one is a heading of its own and shows, so the fold never has to know about sections the stream family renders separately.
static headingId(string $text): stringThe fold ID for a heading whose visible text is $text: lowercase, each run of characters that are neither letters nor digits becomes a single hyphen, and the hyphens at both ends are trimmed. Two headings with the same text share an ID, so folding that ID folds both.
withPreservedNewLines(bool $on = true): selfPreserve consecutive blank lines in source markdown. By default CommonMark collapses runs of blank lines; with this on, every run of blank lines between two blocks survives into render()'s output at the position it held in the source (runs between the items of a list excepted: lists render tight — a dated port decision, see renderList()). Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour.WithPreservedNewLines. The stream family buffers while it is on (defersStreaming()).
withStandardStyle(string $name): selfPick a stock theme by name. Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour.WithStandardStyle. Accepts every name Theme::byName() recognises (the roster is Theme::names(), alias spellings included); unknown names throw InvalidArgumentException listing the valid ones.
withEmoji(bool $on = true): selfExpand :smile:-style emoji shortcodes in rendered text, AFTER parsing: code spans, fenced code and link destinations keep the source bytes (M1). Default off; on, every :shortcode: token in text rewrites through the built-in map. Unknown shortcodes pass through verbatim. Stream and render channels stay byte-identical because the substitution is byte-local to a text run.
withRawControlChars(bool $on = true): selfThe LOUD flag for the control-byte sweep: raw source controls pass through untouched, so every text byte of the document re-opens the ESC / CSI / OSC path to the terminal — a code span may inject an OSC-8 hyperlink or a window-title bait verbatim (FUZZ-03: hostile corpora probe exactly this). Only for trusted input where controls are the payload (e.g. re-emitting captured ANSI art).
withSanitize(bool $on = true): selfStrip C0 / ESC control bytes from source-derived text before emitting it — the safe default. Documented alias of withRawControlChars() read the other way: pass false and you are asking for raw ESC/CSI/OSC re-entry, so prefer the loud name at the call site when you genuinely mean it.
rawControlChars(bool $on = true): self
sanitize(bool $on = true): self

StreamSink final class

Write-through byte sink for the streaming family (Writer, Renderer::writer()).

MethodSummary
static toStream(mixed $resource): selfAdopt a caller-owned writable stream resource. The resource is never closed by this sink.

static ansi(): selfDefault ANSI theme: bright accents on each heading, coloured code, etc.
static plain(): selfPlain-text theme: every Style is a no-op. Colour-free, not glyph-free — the decorative glyphs still draw (see README ## Accessibility). Useful for snapshot tests.
static notty(): selfThe theme fromEnvironment() picks when stdout is not a TTY. Mirrors charmbracelet/glamour.Notty style: indistinguishable from plain() but a separate factory so docs can refer to it by name. Use as the fallback in non-interactive scripts (CI logs, file dumps).
static ascii(): selfMonochrome ASCII theme — every Style emits at most bold / italic / underline / strikethrough (no colour; the strike element carries Style::strikethrough() for ~~text~~). Distinct from plain() (which is a total no-op) and notty() (an alias of plain). Use this when you want emphasis to survive a colourless terminal but not a totally bare one — e.g. printer-friendly logs, accessibility output, or test fixtures that should still differentiate headings from body text.
static names(): arrayThe canonical stock-theme roster — the single source every name list in this library derives from (byName(), requireName(), Renderer::withStandardStyle() errors). Alias spellings (tokyonight, dashed/underscored variants) are accepted by normalisation in byName() but not listed here.
static requireName(string $name): selfStrict sibling of byName(): the same normalised lookup, but an unknown name throws instead of returning null. The message carries the full valid-name list, derived from names().
static byName(string $name): ?selfLook up a built-in theme by glamour-compatible name. Returns null for unknown names so callers can fall back to their own default rather than receiving a surprising one. Names mirror the upstream glamour preset slugs (case-insensitive, hyphens normalised to none); the roster is names(). auto is deliberately NOT a byName slug — it resolves via fromEnvironment() only, so a pure lookup never probes the terminal.
static catalog(): arrayEvery named theme this package ships, keyed by slug: the stock roster (names()) followed by the bundled glamour-style files (solarized, monokai, github). Each entry is loaded once and the same instance is returned on every call.
static catalogByName(string $name): ?selfLook up a theme in catalog() by a loose name: case, hyphens, underscores and spaces are ignored, so Tokyo-Night, tokyo_night and tokyonight name the same theme. Null when nothing answers.
static fromEnvironment(?self $default = null): selfGlamour-compatible env-var auto-selection. NO_COLOR, when set to any non-empty value, wins first (M16): the no-color.org convention asks for plain output regardless of anything else configured, so plain() is returned even against a GLAMOUR_STYLE preset. Otherwise GLAMOUR_STYLE names a preset, and the literal string auto (matching glamour's convention) returns notty() when STDOUT is not a TTY and dark() otherwise. Falls back to $default (default ansi()) when no variable applies or the name is unrecognised. auto probes stream_isatty(STDOUT) only — it never reads TERM, so dumb terminals and screen-reader pipes behind a PTY must pin notty/ascii explicitly (README ## Accessibility). Note that new Renderer() keeps its own ansi() hard default — honouring the environment is exactly what this factory is for.
static dark(): selfDark-background optimised theme. Bright accents for headings, faint code backdrop, blue underlined links — matches glamour's Dark preset visually.
static light(): selfLight-background optimised theme. Darker accents and a no-bg code style.
static dracula(): selfDracula colour scheme — popular dark-purple palette.
static tokyoNight(): selfTokyo Night theme — dark blue/purple palette.
static pink(): selfPink — playful sweet palette.
mapStyles(callable $map): self
with(string $slot, Style $style): selfOne-slot modification idiom: return a copy of this theme with a single Style slot swapped, leaving every other slot (styles and scalars alike) untouched. This is the cheap path for "dark, but gold code" — the constructor's 15 required styles never need re-listing. $slot must name a Style-typed constructor slot; anything else throws with the valid roster.
static fromFile(string $path, ?int $maxBytes = null): selfLoad a theme from a JSON file, optionally bounded by $maxBytes. The JSON shape is one object per element, each carrying a subset of foreground / background (hex #rrggbb or ansi:N or ansi256:N) and the standard boolean attribute flags (bold, italic, underline, strike, faint, blink, reverse) — blink is accepted for glamour parity and discouraged for WCAG 2.2.2 reasons (README ## Accessibility). Missing elements default to the plain Style.
static fromJson(string $path): self
static fromJsonString(string $json): selfDecode a theme from JSON. Two schemas are accepted (M6):

Writer final class

Push-side object channel of the streaming family: feed Markdown chunks as they arrive, and every newly proven top-level section is rendered and written through the StreamSink immediately — write-through flush law, one flush per completed section, no buffering beyond the section stream's own hold.

feed(string $chunk): voidAbsorb one Markdown chunk; newly completed sections are written through to the sink before this returns.
close(): voidDeclare end of document: flush the trailing partial section (terminal flush-partial), drop the final newline run exactly like render() rtrims it, and close the sink. Idempotent.
isOpen(): bool

SectionScanner final class

Pull-agnostic section-splitting state machine for the streaming family (\SugarCraft\Markdown\Renderer::stream() and \SugarCraft\Markdown\Writer, both through SectionStream).

MethodSummary
push(string $chunk): arrayAbsorb one input chunk; answer every section the assembled bytes have newly proven complete (non-blank, in order).
openSection(): stringThe section still being read: everything after the last boundary push() reported, up to the last complete line. When push() has just closed a section, this starts with the heading line that closed it.
finish(): ?stringEnd of document: scan the unterminated trailing line (if any) and return everything not yet returned, or null when it holds no content.

SectionStream final class

Incremental section renderer shared by the streaming family (Renderer::stream(), \SugarCraft\Markdown\Writer) and by any caller that keeps a growing document's rendering between frames.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly Renderer $renderer)
__clone()
push(string $chunk): arrayAbsorb one chunk; answer the bodies of the sections it made final.
finish(): arrayEnd of document: answer every body not answered yet. Held sections are rendered with every definition the document has. Terminal: a stream is not fed after this.
preview(): arrayWhat finish() would answer right now, without disturbing this stream: the frames of a growing reply concatenate their released bodies with this preview and byte-match a full render of everything fed so far. Internally a clone finishes, so the held-section replay (M4) is the same code the real finish runs — no second implementation to drift. The open tail is re-parsed per call; past SectionScanner::MAX_SECTION_BYTES the tail is capped, so an unbounded preview ladder is bounded per frame by construction (SM-S15).
